identified_problem: Transurban is one of the world’s leading toll-road developers and operators, established in Australia in 1996 and operating 22 toll roads across Melbourne, Sydney and Brisbane. The 2019–20 Black Summer bushfires and the 2022 NSW/Queensland floods threatened major road corridors, tunnels and bridges, creating direct asset-damage, traffic-disruption and revenue risks for Transurban’s Australian network.
climate_exposure: Its Australian toll roads, tunnels, bridges and supporting infrastructure are exposed to wildfire, inland flood, storm and heat events across the highly populated east-coast corridor.
potential_pain: Unplanned road closures, repair costs and rising insurance premiums can disrupt toll revenue and strain capital-maintenance budgets; climate-resilience planning requires high-resolution hazard data at the asset level.
evidence: Address-level wildfire and flood exposure layers plus historical event intelligence for the 2019–20 Black Summer and 2022 eastern-Australia floods, mapped to Transurban’s Australian toll-road network.
recommended_message: Show Transurban how Talaix hazard monitoring and historical event intelligence can strengthen asset-level resilience planning for its Australian toll-road network against wildfire and flood.
fit_score: Transurban owns and operates critical transport infrastructure across Australia’s most hazard-exposed east-coast cities, giving it both direct asset risk and a clear operational incentive to invest in hazard analytics.
